wheels.notes: Black Badge: CARB lists a 22 in test configuration for model years 2024 and 2025 beside the 23 in one; which cars got it is not stated. (US page; Canadian cars assumed the same.) DriveClean shows both 22 in and 23 in Black Badge configurations for 2024/2025 without saying which is standard; the NRCan row in the merged data says 22 in, the 23 in comes from the Cars.com 2025 Black Badge page.

Black Badge: 23 in forged wheels (Cars.com 2025 Black Badge page: 23 in, P255/45R23 front / P285/40R23 rear; CARB 23 in configuration covers 2024 and 2025). (US page; Canadian cars assumed the same.) DriveClean shows both 22 in and 23 in Black Badge configurations for 2024/2025 without saying which is standard; the NRCan row in the merged data says 22 in, the 23 in comes from the Cars.com 2025 Black Badge page.

heat_pump.notes: Estimated: ArenaEV lists the Black Badge for 2025-2026 only; the Spectre page (2023-2026) lists the heat pump and the Black Badge shares its battery and climate hardware (101.7 kWh usable on both pages). Years compared: 2024 vs 2025. ArenaEV is a spec database (EU-oriented) and lists the feature as "Yes" without saying standard or optional; read as standard. Rolls-Royce site not usable. ArenaEV lists "Heat pump: Yes" without saying standard or optional (it also says Yes for the 2019–21 i3, where it was a paid option), and its pages mix EU data.
